title: Bridge B · One sound, many spellings
cando: read the long vowel sounds in their different English spellings

about.text: English often writes one long sound in two or three ways. The long a is ai in rain, a_e in name and ay in day. This lesson shows the spellings of the long a, e, i and o sounds, so you can read them.
goals: Read the long a sound: ai, a_e, ay
Read the long e sound: ee, ea
Read the long i sound: ie, i_e, igh
Read the long o sound: oa, o_e, ow
Choose a spelling when you write a word

chapters.title: The long vowels
chapters.text:
This is Bridge B. The long vowels.
So far every vowel was short.
Cat. Pin. Dog. Bus. Short sounds.
Now the vowel says its own name.
Listen. Ai. That is the letter a, long.
Wait. w. ai. t. Three sounds.
Not four. The ai is one sound.
Rain. r. ai. n. Three sounds.
Next. Ee. That is e, long.
Feet. f. ee. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Fit. Feet.
Fit is short. Feet is long.
Next. Ie. That is i, long.
Pie. p. ie. Two sounds only.
Next. Oa. That is o, long.
Boat. b. oa. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Got. Goat.
Last. Oo. This one has two sounds.
Listen. Boot. Now listen. Foot.
Boot is long. Foot is short.
Same two letters. Two sounds.
You cannot tell by looking.
Try the long one first. Then the short one.
One of them will be a word you know.
Now three tricky words.
Who. Love. Have.
These do not follow the sounds.
Who is not w, h, o. It is hoo.
Love does not rhyme with the word rove.
Have does not rhyme with the word gave.
Learn those three by sight.
The vowel says its name.

chapters.title: One sound, more than one spelling
chapters.text:
This lesson has no new sounds at all.
Not one. You have them all.
What it has is new ways to WRITE them.
You know the long a. You met it as ai.
Rain. Wait. That is the sound.
Today you meet two more spellings.
The same sound. Written a different way.
The first is ay. Day. Pay. Away.
It comes at the end of a word.
Ai never comes at the end. Ay does.
That is the whole rule for that one.
The second one is stranger. Listen.
The word man. m. a. n. Short a.
Now I add an e at the end.
M. A. N. E. Mane.
The e is not said. It says nothing.
But it reaches back over the n.
And it makes the a say its name.
Man becomes mane. Tap becomes tape.
Cap becomes cape. Hat becomes hate.
We write this a_e. A, gap, e.
The gap is where one letter goes.
Name. n. a_e. m. Three sounds.
Not four. The e is silent.
Late. l. a_e. t. Three sounds.
So now you have three ways to write long a.
Ai in rain. Ay in day. A_e in name.
Which one does a word use?
You cannot hear it. You have to have seen it.
That is not a fault in you. It is English.
Read a lot and you will know.

sounds.about: Long a, as in day. At the end of a word.
Long o, as in slow. It can also say ow, as in cow.

reader.title: The New Job
reader.text:
I got a job today.
The man said his name.
I must not be late.
So I take the bus at six.
They pay me at the end of the week.
It is not a lot of pay.
But it is a job. I can make it.

canDo: I can read the long a in rain, name and day.
I can read the long e in feet and eat.
I can read the long i in pie, time and night.
I can read the long o in boat, home and slow.
